statement: The Heard Museum's indexed collections description dates some Hopi katsina doll examples to the late nineteenth century and describes publicly shared ceremonial gifting of figures representing Katsinam; these dated museum objects document a collecting horizon, not the origin of Katsina practice.

sources.citation: Heard Museum, 'Hopi Katsina Dolls', collections page https://heard.org/collection/katsina-dolls/
sources.author: Heard Museum
sources.access_note: Museum collection index displayed late-1800s examples, gifting context and materials. Direct page retrieval failed, so museum statement has not been inspected in its full display context.

does_not_demonstrate: Earliest surviving museum dolls cannot date the development of Hopi katsina practice.
Published information about gifts does not authorize documenting private or restricted ceremonies.
Objects collected or made for sale differ from those prepared for community gifting.
adversarial_counter: The searchable museum summary may condense variation among Hopi villages, makers and ritual contexts.
notes: Institutional-source audit. Scope: named public page and its content only; no tradition founding-year inference. Independent historical / community review required before status change.
